**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep eager chat pagination within the production rate budget**

In hosted production, `config/initializers/rack_attack.rb:221-234` allows only 100 `/api/*` requests per bearer token per hour, while `app/controllers/api/v1/chats_controller.rb:10-12` fixes this endpoint at 20 chats per page. This loop performs one request for every page whenever the list is opened or refreshed, so a 1,000-chat account burns 50 requests per refresh and a second refresh can leave every subsequent mobile API call rate-limited for the rest of the window; the 100-page cap can consume the entire budget in one load. Avoid eager page-by-page loading, or make the endpoint honor a larger page size/cursor before fetching the complete list.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve a complete list when a later page fails**

After a complete list has already loaded, any transient failure on page 2 or later takes this branch and returns only the pages accumulated during the failing refresh; `fetchChats` then overwrites `_chats` with that partial result and clears `_errorMessage`. Since `mobile/lib/screens/chat_list_screen.dart:214` only renders an error when the list is empty, older chats silently disappear as though deleted until a later successful refresh. Preserve the previously complete data or return a completeness state and expose a retry affordance.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Respect the requested starting page**

When a caller uses the still-public `page` argument with a value other than 1, the initial request honors it, but this loop always restarts at page 2. For example, `fetchChats(page: 3)` with five pages requests `3, 2, 3, 4, 5`, yielding an out-of-order list that includes pages the caller did not request while omitting page 1 if the new contract is to load everything. Normalize the initial request to page 1/remove the argument, or start follow-up requests after the actual page reported by the first response.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

- **Requested start page** (Codex, CodeRabbit): the follow-up loop now continues from `page + 1` instead of always restarting at page 2, so `fetchChats(page: 3)` requests 3, 4, … in order. Test added.
- **Truncated list on refresh** (Codex): if a later page fails while a list is already on screen, that list is kept instead of being replaced by the partial one. With nothing shown yet the pages loaded so far are still used (existing behaviour, existing test). Test added.
- **Deduplication coverage** (CodeRabbit nitpick): the pagination test now repeats `chat_2` on page 2, so it fails if the `seen` check is removed.

Deliberately left as is, happy to follow the maintainers' preference:

- **Rate budget** (Codex P2): the list is bounded by the existing 100-page cap, but a very large account still costs one request per 20 chats on each refresh. Raising the page size or adding a cursor is an API change, so it seems better as its own PR.
- **"List is partial" notice** (CodeRabbit): needs new UI and strings; also a separate change.
- **Chat deleted while pages load** (CodeRabbit): a narrow race that the next refresh corrects.

This change and its tests were prepared with an AI coding agent (Claude).

Pushed 2f1bddd and 949620d addressing the remaining thread about a chat deleted while later pages are still loading: `fetchChats` now records ids deleted during the fetch (`deleteChat` / `deleteMultipleChats`) and filters them out before assigning the paged list, so they no longer reappear. Each fetch keeps its own set, so two overlapping refreshes no longer interfere. Added regression tests (page 2 held on a Completer with a chat deleted mid-fetch, and two overlapping refreshes); they fail without the change and pass with it, along with the rest of `chat_provider_test.dart`.

Also handled the "show when the chat list is partial" thread (9b8606c): `ChatProvider.hasIncompleteChatList` is set when a later page fails or the 100-page cap truncates the list, and the chat list screen shows a banner with a Try Again action (en/sv strings added); tests cover the failed-page, cap and clear-on-full-refresh cases.

Not changed: resetting chat state on identity change/logout. No provider in the app is reset on logout today and that behaviour predates this PR, so it seems better handled as its own change across providers; happy to open an issue for it if useful.
